name: Leah Acker, MD, PhD (ACkER lab, wearable HRV in older surgical patients)
org: Duke University School of Medicine, Department of Anesthesiology
role: Assistant Professor in Anesthesiology; leads the ACkER lab
why: Her group captures preoperative HRV at home with wrist wearables in adults 65 and older (the HIPPIE study) and reported in 2026 that outpatient wrist HRV capture was feasible for 76.9% of participants. A screenless overnight band reading heart rate and HRV against each wearer's own baseline matches that at home, night time capture problem, and the SDK could pass overnight beat to beat data into their pipeline.
why_now: Feb 2026 paper in the Journal of Cardiovascular Translational Research (Translational Methods for Wearable HRV Monitoring in Older Adults) reports that inpatient wrist data went missing most often in the highest risk patients, the gap an easier overnight band could address.
ask: A 20 minute researcher conversation on what an overnight wrist HRV source would need to be useful for preoperative baselines in older adults, and permission to share SDK docs and sample overnight data once ready.

I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. An overnight band with its own baseline logic and an SDK is a candidate data source for the next round of this rural, shift style workforce research.
why_now: Paper accepted 26 May 2026 in Public Health Challenges (Lessons Learned on the Use of Wearables in Tracking Health Indicators Among Farmworkers in North Carolina) explicitly asks for better suited data collection tools.
